newsitem.title: USA: Aztec in talks to buy 2 galvanizing plants.
newsitem.headline: Aztec in talks to buy 2 galvanizing plants.

text.p: Aztec Manufacturing Co is in discussions to purchase two galvanizing facilities for about $12 million, said Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer L.C. Martin.

Martin told Reuters in a telephone interview the negotiations are at an early stage but he hoped to reach a deal within the next 90 days. He did not say where the two galvanizing facilities are located but said they would tie in with Aztec's eight existing plants in the South and Southwest.
"Our strategic plan is to try to get control of the bulk of the capacity in a geographical area," Martin said.
"We are probably going to be in the $12 million range for both of them (the two facilities)," Martin said.

Aztec earlier this year bought a galvanizing facility in Prairie Grove, Ark. Martin said the plant has boosted revenues from galvanizing operations, and "significantly impacted our bottom line in a positive manner."

Martin said Aztec had net income of about $875,000, or $0.15 per share, in the fiscal second quarter ended Aug. 31, compared with $0.10 per share last year. Preliminary figures showed total sales were up from $11 million to about $13.5 million.

Martin said the second half of fiscal 1997 should also be firm. He said total revenues in the third quarter "will probably be close to what they were in the second quarter ...They should be up a little but not very much."

Martin said Aztec has improved its margins in its electrical products segment, which accounts for about 50 percent of revenues, by making organizational changes at its Calvert Co unit in Jackson, Miss.
